annotation.authors_or_issuer: Yoon, H.; Kim, M.-G.; Park, C.; Ahn, H.-N.
annotation.summary_en: Preprint proposing "psychological boundaries" as a mechanism governing visitors' openness to robot intervention, and a cost-sensitive, boundary-aware interaction policy for exhibition service robots. Based on a survey of 164 visitors, it finds three service-preference dimensions and argues robots should show situational restraint to respect visitor autonomy. It is a design study, not a governance instrument.
key_provisions_or_claims: Visitor service preferences fall into three dimensions: proactive support, adaptive responsiveness, and autonomy-oriented minimal service.
Hedonic and epistemic motivations shape the permeability of psychological boundaries.
A cost-sensitive decision model accounts for asymmetric misclassification costs.
Early classification of visitor type from minimal inputs enables selection of service intensity.
Robotic intelligence includes restraint: withholding intervention to respect visitor autonomy.
annotation.title_clean: Navigating Psychological Boundaries: A Boundary-Aware Interaction Policy for Adaptive Service Robots in Exhibitions
annotation.title_en: Navigating Psychological Boundaries: A Boundary-Aware Interaction Policy for Adaptive Service Robots in Exhibitions
